post.title: Structured Agent Environments
post.hook: A 43-line README cut a coding agent's token bill by 36%. Then came AGENTS.md.
post.summary: A measurement harness that runs a coding agent on fixed tasks under six levels of project context and records token cost. The pilot already shows context pays for itself on T01.
post.writeup:
## What it is
A research rig for one question: does richer project context let a coding agent orient faster and spend fewer tokens, without hurting task success? It runs a coding agent against 10 fixed tasks (T01 to T10) cut from a pinned snapshot of the xo-cowork-api repo.

## The conditions
Six environments, from E0 (empty workspace) through E1 (README only), E2 (AGENTS.md only), E3 (AGENTS.md plus PROJECT.md), E4 (full XO scaffold with empty memory) to E5 (full scaffold plus seeded memory). Each task, environment and replication is one cell, and each cell yields one telemetry record: tokens, timing, navigation, operations and an acceptance-criteria score.

## How it works
Shell scripts create an isolated worktree per run, apply the environment overlay, launch the agent, then extract telemetry from the transcript, grade the diff and remove the worktree. Analysis scripts flatten everything into a parquet dataset, compute derived metrics, run statistics with BCa bootstrap confidence intervals (10,000 samples), and generate 12 figures. Later work made the harness hermetic and multi-operator, with a tag per operator so collaborators can run slices and merge results.

## Results so far
The pilot is 60 cells (10 tasks × 6 environments × 1 agent). On T01, input tokens fell from 2,203,107 in the empty workspace to 1,403,820 with a README and 1,272,483 with AGENTS.md. Shell commands dropped from 68 to 44 to 42, while file reads stayed near 13 to 17. All three scored 1.0.

On T02 and T03, the agent often did only two of three acceptance criteria, scoring 0.667 in the leaner environments.

## Open questions
Only T01 has a complete row so far. Heavy parallel codex runs hit the 900 s cap and logged 0 tokens for the richest cells. The full study (360 runs) is needed to tell whether the E3 to E5 scaffolds and memory add anything beyond a good README.

slides.heading: Does a 43-line README really make an agent cheaper?
slides.body: A harness that measures coding-agent cost under six levels of project context.

slides.heading: T01 input tokens by environment
slides.takeaway: Three of six environments shown: context cut tokens while every run still scored 1.0.

slides.heading: Six environments, from empty to seeded memory

slides.text: A 43-line README cuts token use by 36%. Adding AGENTS.md gets another 6%. The savings come from fewer shell explorations, not fewer file reads.

slides.heading: Context buys orientation, not just answers
slides.body: On T01 the agent explored less with a README, and only one task row is done, so the full 360-run study decides the rest.
